Jonas / Marissa — ran quick tiling math in the workbook. Summary of recommended options (high level):

Option A — Dedicated reserved pool (fastest predictable latency)
- Tile: 12xA10 equivalent (reserved) + 4xA10 burst capacity (on-demand)
- Expected headroom: handles sustained 250 rps with P95 ~260–320ms; burst ladder to 380 rps using on-demand tiles with degraded latency to ~420ms at extreme spikes.
- Monthly commit delta (pilot vs reserved conversion): pilot 3-month cost estimate $76k/month (staged rate), reserved 12-month $62k/month effective.
- Ops notes: simpler monitoring, clearer SLA, tighter KV-cache locality for latency.

Option B — Private VPC deployment with reserved control plane + mixed GPU carve-outs
- Tile: 8xA10 reserved (VPC tenancy) + 6xA10 preemptible/burst pool (private burst within their VPC overlay)
- Expected headroom: sustained ~180–220 rps at P95 ~330–380ms; better compliance posture (customer KMS, network controls). Burstable to 380 rps if preemptible pool is healthy; risk of reduced availability for burst.
- Monthly cost: pilot ~68k/month, reserved 12-month effective ~58k/month.
- Ops notes: additional onboarding for network, KMS integration, periodic evidence package for SOC2/PHI traceability.

Recommendations (short):
1) Start with Option B for the 3-month pilot: meets compliance ask, fits procurement staged commitment, slightly lower pilot cost.
2) Include an explicit burst SLA addendum and pre-warmed node ladder in the contract (AMM): e.g., 4 pre-warmed on-demand tiles triggered automatically at spikes >300 rps for >5 minutes.
3) If after pilot we see consistent P95 <350ms and >250 sustained rps, convert to Option A reserved commit for cost predictability and tighter latency.

I updated cv_gpu_tiling_v1.xlsx with numeric rows on the "CareVault_slate" tab. Also flagged required security evidence in the workbook.

-Karthik

Lena / CareVault procurement — appreciate the clarity. Attaching a short pilot M.A.P. and a draft SLA addendum (cv_sla_draft.pdf) that includes the AMM burst ladder Karthik suggested and an evidence checklist for security controls.

Pilot mutual action plan (3 months):
1) Week 0–1: Network & KMS onboarding (Evelyn will drive), access & evidence exchange.
2) Week 1–2: Private VPC deployment / pre-warm step, baseline load testing at 70/150/300 rps.
3) Week 3–12: Run pilot under Option B configuration (8x reserved + 6x burst pool). Weekly run-rate reports, token-level cost breakdown, and the P95 latency dashboard shared.
4) Week 10: Decision checkpoint — convert to 12-month reserved (Option A) vs continue Private VPC with staged commits. Conversion mechanics: 30-day notice + pro-rated credit for pilot commit.

Contract highlights:
- Pilot monthly fee: $68,000 (Option B configuration).
- Burst AMM: auto-trigger up to 4 on-demand tiles for spikes >300 rps sustained >5m. Burst usage billed at on-demand rates.
- Security: Redwood to provide SOC2 artifact subset + security_evidence_summary.docx within 3 business days of onboarding; additional PHI airgap work scoped separately.
